machine: Apple M1 Max, 32 GB unified memory, macOS 26.6.2, Apple Swift 6.4
scope: Rejected probe: Metal FlashAttention (philipturner/metal-flash-attention, MIT, main at probe time) forward kernel at Qwen-Image-2.1's cached 1024 shape, as a replacement for MPSGraph SDPA
harness: Throwaway SwiftPM executable in the session scratchpad; one dispatch per head in one command buffer; GPU timestamps; median of 5-7 runs; head 0 checked against a CPU FP64 reference on every 97th row
compiler_finding: MFA's generated source relies on private air.simdgroup_async_copy_* and air.wait_simdgroup_events intrinsics, which this Metal compiler rejects ('illegal string literal in asm'). They were replaced by a synchronous lane-strided copy with identical semantics so the kernel could run.
accuracy: head 0 nRMSE versus FP64 1.1e-06 to 1.25e-06 with FP32 intermediates (6.5e-04 with FP16 intermediates); MPSGraph SDPA measures 4.9e-04 against scalar FP32
decision: Rejected. Without the removed asynchronous-copy intrinsics MFA reaches 4.75 TFLOP/s at best, slower than MPSGraph before counting the head-major layout conversions it would need. MPSGraph SDPA remains the 1024 attention path. The published 83% M1 Max utilization depends on those intrinsics.
